query: Starting from a W–Cu composite containing W particles or interconnected W ligaments within a Cu matrix, what single intervention could overcome phase separation and interfacial void formation, thereby improving thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under heat-transfer and irradiation conditions relevant to joints between W-based plasma-facing materials and Cu-based cooling components? Formulate one hypothesis that states the intervention, the proposed mechanism, the predicted comparative outcome, the applicable processing and service boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Friction stir processing (FSP) of the W–Cu composite will induce a graded interfacial zone that mitigates phase separation and reduces the formation of interfacial voids, thereby enhancing its thermal conductivity under high heat-flux and irradiation conditions.
generation.material_initial_state: A W–Cu composite containing tungsten particles or interconnected tungsten ligaments dispersed within a copper matrix, which in the untreated state exhibits phase separation and interfacial voids.
generation.intervention: Application of friction stir processing (FSP) under controlled temperature and strain conditions.
generation.conditions: Processing and service conditions relevant to joints between tungsten-based plasma-facing materials and copper-based cooling components; specifically, exposure to high heat flux and irradiation environments similar to reactor divertor or similar high-energy settings.
generation.structural_mediator: A graded, diffusion-mediated interfacial layer (or core–shell structure) between the W and Cu phases produced during FSP.
generation.mechanism: FSP mechanically stirs and locally heats the material, promoting atomic interdiffusion at the W–Cu interfaces. This leads to the development of a graded interfacial microstructure that suppresses phase separation and minimizes void formation, thereby improving the continuity for heat transfer across the interface even under irradiation.
generation.predicted_outcome: The FSP-treated composite is expected to exhibit a statistically significant reduction in interfacial void density and an increase in effective thermal conductivity relative to the untreated composite under simulated service conditions.
generation.baseline: The untreated W–Cu composite which shows detrimental phase separation and interfacial voids that limit thermal transfer efficiency.
generation.boundary: FSP parameters must be optimized to avoid overheating (i.e., temperatures must remain below the melting point of copper and avoid degradation of tungsten), and the improvements are claimed under the specific joint conditions between plasma-facing and cooling components, particularly under heat-transfer and irradiation exposures typical of reactor environments.
generation.uncertainty: The exact magnitude of thermal conductivity enhancement and long-term stability under extended irradiation remain uncertain. The scalability of FSP for large joint areas and prolonged service-life effects are also not fully established.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identical W–Cu composite samples. Subject one set to friction stir processing under optimized conditions and leave the other set untreated. Characterize the interfacial microstructure using high-resolution electron microscopy and quantify void density via image analysis. Subject both sample groups to simulated service conditions that include high heat flux and controlled irradiation. Measure thermal conductivity before and after exposure using standard thermal property measurement techniques.
measurements: Interfacial void density (via electron microscopy and image analysis)
Interfacial composition gradients (via EDS or similar techniques)
Thermal conductivity (using laser flash analysis or similar methods) before and after simulated service conditions
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the friction stir processed samples do not display a statistically significant reduction in interfacial void density and do not demonstrate improved thermal conductivity relative to the untreated samples after exposure to high heat flux and irradiation conditions, then the hypothesis that FSP improves the interfacial structure and thermal performance is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: (1) The AlCoCrFeNi/A356 composite with a uniform particle distribution and limited interface reaction can be fabricated by friction stir processing. The core–shell structure between the HEA particles and the Al matrix in the composite can be controlled via atomic diffusion at high temperature. (2) The shell zone of the interface consists of two different layers with different microstructure and element distribution, and the formation of a gradient microstructure depends on the solution diffusion and the crystal structure of HEA alloys. (3) Microstructure and composition gradients benefit the movement of dislocation, and excellent mechanical properties can be obtained for the FSPed AMCs under an optimum solution treatment condition.

In this study, AZ91 magnesium-alloy-based metal matrix composites (MMCs) reinforced with 10 wt% of Al0.5CoCrFeNi2 high-entropy alloy (HEA) particles and SiC particles were prepared by a spark plasma sintering (SPS) process at 300 °C. The effects of reinforcements on the microstructure and mechanical properties of AZ91-based MMCs were studied. The results showed that AZ91–HEA composite consisted of α-Mg, Mg17Al12 and FCC phases. No interfacial reaction layer was observed between HEA particles and the Mg matrix. After adding HEA into AZ91, the compressive yield strength (C.Y.S) of the AZ91–HEA composite increased by 17% without degradation of failure strain. In addition, the increment in C.Y.S brought by HEA was comparable to that contributed by commonly used SiC reinforcement (15%). A relatively low porosity in the composite and enhanced interfacial bonding between the α-Mg matrix and HEA particles make HEA a potential reinforcement material in MMCs.
